# Ohio Drum Major Resigns Amid Controversy Over Presidential Nod

(CNN) -- An Ohio man suspended as drum major of his band for acknowledging President Obama during last week's inaugural parade has announced his resignation. John Coleman stepped down from the Cleveland Firefighters Memorial Pipes & Drums a week after the Washington parade, citing the overwhelming publicity surrounding his suspension.

"It's come to a point where I don't want embarrassment anymore between the pipe band and myself," Coleman, a firefighter by profession, told CNN affiliate WEWS on Tuesday.

During the nationally televised January 20 parade, Coleman was observed nodding toward the newly inaugurated president while marching with the band, followed moments later by what appeared to be a brief wave. According to Coleman, the exchange occurred naturally as the band passed the grandstand where Obama was seated.

"Contact was made with our eyes both together and he smiled and waved at the band," Coleman explained to WEWS. "And just as a gesture, I nodded my head. I gave him a slight wave and went on."

*Watch parade and explanation »*

CNN's attempts to reach representatives from the band were unsuccessful. However, bandleader Mike Engle told the *Cleveland Plain Dealer* that Coleman's suspension stemmed from a breach of military protocol. "We had gone over and over time and again with everyone in the band that this was a military parade," Engle explained. "Protocol and proper decorum had to be followed at all times. Unfortunately, John chose to ignore that." Coleman had received a six-month suspension from the band.

In a written statement, band manager Ken Rybka described Coleman's resignation as "a shock and surprise." He noted that since the story broke on Monday, the band had been inundated with phone calls, emails, and online messages—the vast majority expressing criticism.

*iReport.com: 'Pretty cool thing that he acknowledged the president'*

"It is unfortunate that an internal band issue has raised so much discussion and ire from the general public," Rybka stated. "It has disheartened me more than you can imagine."

Rybka further announced that he would be taking a leave of absence from the band in light of the controversy. "The 'afterglow' of participating in the inaugural parade is gone," he remarked.
